items.source: Linux real Electron GUI + deterministic media.stage hold; source worktree on e40c896a1876c9f6c4115c6267e96b16e2564e0a
items.symptom: Rejected asynchronous paste inserts no stale image and publishes no reference, but an unreferenced staged PNG/settings metadata survives independent PID restart. Needs I3 contract assessment; inventory tracks staged resource, so this is not an untracked-file or cross-card data-loss claim.
items.rootCause: media.stage allocated tracked settings/media-draft and file before insertion; renderer rejected obsolete paste without releasing host resource. Prior no-auto-delete contract had no request ownership or recovery lease.
items.verification: Linux formal Electron PASS, including SIGKILL/new PID; Windows NOT_RUN

contractReview.interpretation: Tracked media-draft settings + file, not an untracked assets-table row. stageImage allocates a fresh UUID per operation. No usage reference found in captured SQLite state. Existing contract explicitly retains staged resources; no automatic deletion implemented. Concurrent in-flight usage has no request-scoped lease/ownership token in the existing protocol.

contracts.quote: 媒体服务暂存后不自动删除，避免破坏历史。
暂存资源不能因插入失败擅删，以免破坏其它历史引用

contractReview.decision: Keep FAIL and request contract review; do not introduce renderer-side broad deletion or weaken FAULT-05. Future change needs request-scoped staging ownership + host-side reference/transaction guard + crash recovery semantics.

items.minimalFix: Opt-in per-paste insertionId; host allocates fresh IDs and durably journals each filename/hash before first write. Finish accepted retains resources; finish rejected retires only matching request ownership and hash after comprehensive persistent-reference check. Pending assets hidden from resource picker. Cleanup occurs after durable command receipt; failure is queryable/logged and retries on commands or owner-lock startup. Startup recovers pending requests only, not all orphan media.

contractResolution.decision: Request-owned rejected insertion resources may be reclaimed only after reference/ownership/hash checks; accepted and ordinary staged resources retain existing lifecycle.
